1: use ruff_diagnostics::{Diagnostic, Edit, Fix, FixAvailability, Violation};
2: use ruff_macros::{derive_message_formats, ViolationMetadata};
3: use ruff_python_trivia::CommentRanges;
4: use ruff_source_file::{LineRanges, UniversalNewlineIterator};
5: use ruff_text_size::TextRange;
6: 
7: use crate::settings::LinterSettings;
8: use crate::Locator;
9: 
10: use super::super::detection::comment_contains_code;
11: 
12: /// ## What it does
13: /// Checks for commented-out Python code.
14: ///
15: /// ## Why is this bad?
16: /// Commented-out code is dead code, and is often included inadvertently.
17: /// It should be removed.
18: ///
19: /// ## Known problems
20: /// Prone to false positives when checking comments that resemble Python code,
21: /// but are not actually Python code ([#4845]).
22: ///
23: /// ## Example
24: /// ```python
25: /// # print("Hello, world!")
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## Options
29: /// - `lint.task-tags`
30: ///
31: /// [#4845]: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/4845
32: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
33: pub(crate) struct CommentedOutCode;
34: 
35: impl Violation for CommentedOutCode {
36:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::None;
37: 
38:     #[derive_message_formats]
39:     fn message(&self) -> String {
40:         "Found commented-out code".to_string()
41:     }
42: 
43:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
44:         Some("Remove commented-out code".to_string())
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: /// ERA001
49: pub(crate) fn commented_out_code(
50:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
51:     locator: &Locator,
52:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
53:     settings: &LinterSettings,
54: ) {
55:     let scanner = ScriptTagScanner { locator };
56:     let mut comments = comment_ranges.into_iter().peekable();
57:     // Iterate over all comments in the document.
58:     while let Some(range) = comments.next() {
59:         let line = locator.line_str(range.start());
60: 
61:         if is_script_tag_start(line) {
62:             if scanner.skip_script_comments(range, &mut comments, comment_ranges) {
63:                 continue;
64:             }
65:         }
66: 
67:         // Verify that the comment is on its own line, and that it contains code.
68:         if is_own_line_comment(line) && comment_contains_code(line, &settings.task_tags[..]) {
69:             let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(CommentedOutCode, range);
70:             diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::display_only_edit(Edit::range_deletion(
71:                 locator.full_lines_range(range),
72:             )));
73:             diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
74:         }
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: struct ScriptTagScanner<'a> {
79:     locator: &'a Locator<'a>,
80: }
81: 
82: impl<'a> ScriptTagScanner<'a> {
83:     /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
84:     /// script comment and moves `comments` past the script comment's end unless
85:     /// the script comment is invalid.
86:     ///
87:     /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
88:     fn skip_script_comments<I>(
89:         &self,
90:         script_start: TextRange,
91:         comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
92:         comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
93:     ) -> bool
94:     where
95:         I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
96:     {
97:         let contents = self.locator.contents();
98:         let line_index = self.locator.to_index();
99:         let tag_start = script_start.start();
100:         let tag_end = script_start.end();
101:         let tag_location = line_index.source_location(tag_end, contents);
102:         let recovered = line_index.offset(tag_location.row, tag_location.column, contents);
103:         let position = if recovered == tag_end {
104:             recovered
105:         } else {
106:             tag_end
107:         };
108: 
109:         let line_starts = line_index.line_starts();
110:         let row_index = tag_location.row.to_zero_indexed();
111:         let line_end = if line_index.is_ascii() {
112:             if row_index + 1 >= line_starts.len() {
113:                 self.locator.text_len()
114:             } else {
115:                 line_starts[row_index + 1]
116:             }
117:         } else {
118:             self.locator.full_line_end(position)
119:         };
120:         let rest = self.locator.after(line_end);
121:         let mut end_offset = None;
122:         let mut lines = UniversalNewlineIterator::with_offset(rest, line_end);
123: 
124:         while let Some(line) = lines.next() {
125:             let Some(content) = script_line_content(line.as_str()) else {
126:                 break;
127:             };
128: 
129:             let is_terminator = if line_index.is_ascii() {
130:                 content.as_bytes() == b"///"
131:             } else {
132:                 content == "///"
133:             };
134: 
135:             if is_terminator {
136:                 // > Precedence for an ending line # /// is given when the next line is not a valid
137:                 // > embedded content line as described above.
138:                 // > For example, the following is a single fully valid block:
139:                 // > ```python
140:                 // > # /// some-toml
141:                 // > # embedded-csharp = """
142:                 // > # /// <summary>
143:                 // > # /// text
144:                 // > # ///
145:                 // > # /// </summary>
146:                 // > # public class MyClass { }
147:                 // > # """
148:                 // > # ///
149:                 // ````
150:                 if lines.next().is_some_and(|line| is_valid_script_line(line.as_str())) {
151:                     continue;
152:                 }
153:                 end_offset = Some(line.full_end());
154:                 break;
155:             }
156:         }
157: 
158:         // > Unclosed blocks MUST be ignored.
159:         let Some(end_offset) = end_offset else {
160:             return false;
161:         };
162: 
163:         // Skip over all script-comments recorded for this block.
164:         let enclosed = comment_ranges.comments_in_range(TextRange::new(tag_start, end_offset));
165:         let block_end = enclosed
166:             .last()
167:             .map_or(end_offset, |comment| comment.end().max(end_offset));
168: 
169:         while let Some(comment) = comments.peek() {
170:             if comment.start() >= block_end {
171:                 break;
172:             }
173: 
174:             comments.next();
175:         }
176: 
177:         true
178:     }
179: }
180: 
181: fn script_line_content(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
182:     let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix('#') else {
183:         // Not a comment
184:         return None;
185:     };
186: 
187:     // An empty line
188:     if rest.is_empty() {
189:         return Some("");
190:     }
191: 
192:     // > If there are characters after the # then the first character MUST be a space.
193:     rest.strip_prefix(' ')
194: }
195: 
196: fn is_valid_script_line(line: &str) -> bool {
197:     script_line_content(line).is_some()
198: }
199: 
200: /// Returns `true` if line contains an own-line comment.
201: fn is_own_line_comment(line: &str) -> bool {
202:     for char in line.chars() {
203:         if char == '#' {
204:             return true;
205:         }
206:         if !char.is_whitespace() {
207:             return false;
208:         }
209:     }
210:     unreachable!("Comment should contain '#' character")
211: }
212: 
213: /// Returns `true` if the line appears to start a script tag.
214: ///
215: /// See: <https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/>
216: fn is_script_tag_start(line: &str) -> bool {
217:     line == "# /// script"
218: }
